title: Second Sound in Solids
authors: Marvin Chester
read_scope: All 3 PDF pages; first begins with final text of unrelated article
model_constitutive: Maxwell–Cattaneo relaxation: τ q_t+q=−K grad T; heat balance C T_t=−div q
geometry: Homogeneous rigid dielectric/insulating solid; bulk thermal waves
method: Macroscopic heat-flux and balance derivation, phonon-gas speed argument
main_result: Damped thermal wave, threshold frequency 1/(2πτ); estimated τ=3K/(C s²) and speed s/√3
validation: Low-frequency equation reduces to Fourier diffusion; the speed argument is compared to known phonon-gas theory, not an experimental validation
stated_limitations: No spatial pressure/density gradients; phonon-gas extension of kinetic arguments is hypothesized; τ estimate assumes phonon heat transport and idealized nondispersive isotropic speed; temperature loses meaning beyond equilibration rate
future_work: Authors report experiments underway, especially low-temperature KCl

title: Generalized thermoelasticity for anisotropic media
authors: Ranjit S. Dhaliwal; Hani H. Sherief
model_constitutive: Anisotropic local thermoelastic stress; Lord–Shulman-type single relaxation q_i+τ q̇_i=−k_ij θ_,j
geometry: General bounded anisotropic body; mixed displacement/traction and fixed-temperature boundary for uniqueness
method: Linear thermodynamic derivation, uniqueness energy argument, variational formulation
main_result: Anisotropic generalization; uniqueness under stated positivity and regularity; corresponding variational principle
validation: Analytic isotropic reduction to Lord–Shulman; no numerical or experimental validation
stated_limitations: Linearized theory near reference temperature; theorem assumes specified homogeneous data, regularity, positive density, heat capacity and elastic quadratic form; equations may contain PDF extraction errors
future_work: Not explicitly stated in inspected paper

title: Experimental Support for the Lagging Behavior in Heat Propagation
authors: Da Yu Tzou
journal: Journal of Thermophysics and Heat Transfer
model_constitutive: Rigid-conductor dual-phase-lag (DPL) heat conduction q(r, t + tau_q) = -K grad T(r, t + tau_T) with energy -div q = C_p dT/dt; Taylor-expanded to 1st/2nd order reducing to diffusion, CV-wave, Jeffreys, parabolic/hyperbolic two-step, and Guyer-Krumhansl limits.
geometry: 1D thin gold film (femtosecond laser heating) and 1D semi-infinite superfluid liquid helium (temperature pulse)
method: Laplace transform in time with analytical spatial solution and Riemann-sum numerical Laplace inversion
main_result: DPL reproduces ultrafast gold-film transient temperature response (with tau_q < tau_T, heat flux preceding temperature gradient due to phonon-electron coupling) and smooths CV wavefront corners into bell-shaped pulses matching liquid He II traces (with tau_T < tau_q).
validation: Quantitative comparison against femtosecond laser-heating experiments on gold films (Brorson et al. 1987; Qiu and Tien 1992; Qiu et al. 1994) and superfluid He II pulse oscilloscope traces (Bertman and Sandiford 1970); analytical reductions to 6 limiting models.
stated_limitations: Uses equilibrium temperature concept as an engineering approximation during ultra-short nonequilibrium transitions; general closed-form solution of exact delay PDE with unexpanded shifts tau_T, tau_q is not known.
future_work: Analyze physical cause-and-effect precedence (tau_T > tau_q vs tau_T < tau_q) across substructural delay mechanisms using the Boltzmann transport equation.

title: An Introduction to the Theory of Piezoelectricity (Second Edition)
authors: Jiashi Yang
journal: Advances in Mechanics and Mathematics Vol. 9 (Springer)
read_scope: frontmatter, TOC, Ch. 5 rod vibrations, Ch. 7 thermal/nonlocal/gradient effects, index (287 pp. monograph)
model_constitutive: 3D nonlinear electroelasticity (Tiersten two-continuum model) and IEEE-standard linear piezoelectricity; Ch. 7 adds linear/nonlinear thermopiezoelectricity, semiconduction, Eringen-type nonlocal dielectric kernel K(x-x') = (1/2alpha)exp(-|x-x'|/alpha) reduced on [0,h] to differential form, strain/polarization gradients, and full Maxwell coupling.
geometry: 3D general continua, rods, ceramic/quartz plates, cylinders, half-spaces, layered/jointed plates, thin dielectric film [0,h]
method: Variational principles, displacement-potential and four-vector formulations, harmonic plane/surface/guided wave eigenproblems, Fredholm integral-to-ODE reduction for bounded nonlocal thin film
main_result: Unified textbook derivation of 3D nonlinear/linear piezoelectricity, biasing-field incremental theory, exact wave/vibration solutions, and bounded-domain nonlocal thin-film capacitance C/C0 < 1 showing boundary-layer field enhancement near electrodes.
validation: Analytical recovery of local/classical limits (e.g., C/C0 -> 1 as h/alpha -> infinity, classical Rayleigh/Love/Bleustein-Gulyaev limits).
stated_limitations: Scope explicitly restricted mainly to exact 3D piezoelectric theory without pre-existing fields in Chs. 2-5; 1D/2D structural beam/plate/shell approximations deferred to other monographs.
future_work: Extensions beyond Ch. 1 framework (thermal, dissipative, semiconducting, nonlocal, gradient, full electromagnetic couplings) introduced only as brief introductory formulations in Ch. 7.

title: The Linear Theory of Micropolar Thermoelasticity
authors: T. R. Tauchert; W. D. Claus Jr.; T. Ariman
model_constitutive: Linear isotropic and anisotropic micropolar thermoelasticity (Eringen micropolar balance laws + Clausius-Duhem inequality + Fourier heat law q_i = k theta_,i); couple stress m_kl independent of temperature in linear isotropic case.
geometry: General 3D bounded regular domain D with boundary B
method: Coleman-Noll thermodynamic restriction, displacement-microrotation (7 PDEs) and stress-couple-stress (19 unknowns + Sandru compatibility) formulations, energy-integral uniqueness proofs, body-force analogy, Goodier-type potential reduction
main_result: Constructs linear micropolar thermoelastic constitutive and field equations, proves uniqueness for coupled dynamic and uncoupled quasistatic BVPs, extends Duhamel-Neumann body-force analogy, and reduces uncoupled problems to isothermal micropolar elasticity via Poisson equations.
validation: Reduces to isothermal micropolar elasticity (Eringen 1966) when theta=0 and to classical linear thermoelasticity when coupling modulus kappa=0.
stated_limitations: Linear constant-property theory with classical Fourier conduction (infinite thermal speed); thermomechanical coupling neglected in sections 3.2-5 except where thermoelastic dissipation is primary.
future_work: Solve particular boundary-value problems including temperature effects to suggest experimental tests confirming or disproving micropolar thermoelasticity in granular media.

title: Wave reflection by the free boundary of a microstructured flexoelectric half-space
authors: Baljeet Singh; Geetika Gupta
journal: Mechanics Based Design of Structures and Machines
read_scope: title, abstract, governing equations (pp. 1-3), numerical results & conclusion (pp. 10-23)
model_constitutive: 2D centrosymmetric isotropic dielectric with strain-gradient elasticity (length scale l), micro-inertia -(1/3)rho_0 n^2 grad^2 u_tt, polarization gradients (a_12, a_44, a_77), and direct/converse static bulk flexoelectricity (f^d, f^c); isothermal (no thermal field).
geometry: 2D semi-infinite half-space (x3 >= 0) with stress-free plane boundary
method: Harmonic plane-wave ansatz reducing 4 coupled PDEs (u, w, P1, P3) to quadratic dispersion in V*^2; analytical reflection amplitude ratios and energy flux shares for incident qP and qSV waves
main_result: Identifies two dispersive plane waves (qP, qSV) slowed by micro-inertia and bulk flexoelectricity; reflected qP wave vanishes beyond critical qSV incidence angle theta_c = 28 deg; kl, n/l, and flexoelectricity strongly affect qP reflection near 60-70 deg.
validation: Energy conservation check (sum of reflected energy ratios <= 1 at all incident angles) and qualitative agreement with Qi (2019) for strontium titanate parameters.
stated_limitations: Restricted to 2D isothermal isotropic centrosymmetric half-space with static bulk flexoelectricity; for incident qSV wave, kl, n/l, and f have negligible effect on reflection/energy ratios.
future_work: None explicitly stated beyond nanoscale flexoelectric device/characterization relevance.

title: Propagation and attenuation of Rayleigh waves in generalized thermoelastic media
authors: M. D. Sharma
read_scope: title, abstract, intro, fundamental equations (pp. 61-64), conclusions & references (pp. 77-79)
model_constitutive: Unified 3D/2D isotropic generalized thermoelasticity covering Lord-Shulman (epsilon=1, single relaxation tau_0) and Green-Lindsay (epsilon=0, two relaxations tau_1 >= tau_0 >= 0) via Helmholtz potentials.
geometry: 2D/3D homogeneous isotropic half-space (z >= 0) with stress-free isothermal or thermally insulated plane boundary
method: Currie-type polynomial rationalization of complex irrational secular dispersion equation, numerical root-finding with radiation/decay filtering to remove spurious roots, depth-dependent particle-motion polarization analysis
main_result: Exact complex roots yield phase speed, attenuation, and elliptical/tilted particle trajectories for copper and limestone; insulated boundary can cause rectilinear surface motion and large changes in attenuation; no second (additional) thermoelastic Rayleigh mode found.
validation: Filters extraneous polynomial roots against original radical secular equation and depth-decay radiation condition; checks low/high-frequency behavior across copper and limestone.
stated_limitations: Homogeneous isotropic linear thermoelasticity only; unlike viscoelasticity (Currie et al. 1977), no additional Rayleigh surface wave root was found for the chosen thermoelastic models.
future_work: Investigate existence of additional Rayleigh surface waves in thermoviscoelastic materials using the rationalized dispersion framework.

title: Heat waves
authors: D. D. Joseph; Luigi Preziosi
read_scope: title, abstract, TOC, Secs. I-II (pp. 41-43), Sec. VIII-IX concluding remarks & references (pp. 69-73)
model_constitutive: Comprehensive review of linear/nonlinear rigid-conductor heat-wave constitutive laws: Cattaneo telegraph law, Jeffreys-type effective thermal conductivity + memory kernel q = -k1 grad theta - int Q(t-t') grad theta dt', Guyer-Krumhansl, Gurtin-Pipkin internal-energy/heat-flux memory, Coleman-Fabrizio-Owen nonlinear Cattaneo.
geometry: Rigid heat conductors (1D pulses, half-space sudden heating, melt interfaces, dielectric crystals, liquid He II)
method: Boltzmann/kinetic, viscoelastic-analogy relaxation-kernel, random-walk, thermodynamic, and canonical wave/characteristic analyses plus annotated historical bibliography
main_result: Shows how fast-relaxing modes create an effective Fourier conductivity that singularly perturbs slower heat waves, explaining why diffusion dominates except at cryogenic second-sound windows (He II, NaF, Bi) or sub-relaxation timescales.
validation: Analytical canonical solutions and synthesis against classical cryogenic second-sound experiments (Peshkov, Ackerman, McNelly, Narayanamurti-Dynes) and MD shock studies (Tsai-MacDonald).
stated_limitations: Confined primarily to rigid conductors (deformations set to zero); notes that almost nothing is known about history dependence of internal energy and room-temperature relaxation times are too short for contemporaneous oscilloscopes.
future_work: Resolve melt-interface temperature jump vs singular Renardy-type kernels in Gurtin-Pipkin hyperbolic Stefan problems; measure history dependence of internal energy and ultra-short-time wave speeds.

title: A Higher-Order Nonlocal Elasticity and Strain Gradient Theory and Its Applications in Wave Propagation
authors: C. W. Lim; G. Zhang; J. N. Reddy
journal: Journal of the Mechanics and Physics of Solids
read_scope: title, abstract, intro (pp. 1-6), thermodynamic model derivation (pp. 8-10), MD comparison & conclusions (pp. 25-31)
model_constitutive: Higher-order nonlocal strain gradient elasticity (NSGT): stored energy depends nonlocally on both strain epsilon_kl (kernel alpha_0, parameter e0*a) and first strain gradient epsilon_kl,m (kernel alpha_1, parameter e1*a) plus material gradient length l; isothermal.
geometry: 3D continuum specialized to 1D Euler-Bernoulli and Timoshenko nanobeams (carbon nanotubes)
method: Thermodynamic/Clausius-Duhem framework with Polizzotto nonlocal residuals, variational derivation of higher-order PDEs and BCs, analytical harmonic flexural dispersion relations
main_result: Unifies softening Eringen nonlocal stress and stiffening strain-gradient effects into one differential beam dispersion law with critical and cut-off wavenumbers, capturing both long-wavelength stiffness enhancement and high-wavenumber phase-velocity roll-off.
validation: Exact reductions to pure Eringen nonlocal stress (l=0) and pure strain-gradient elasticity (e0=e1=0); quantitative dispersion benchmarked against CNT molecular dynamics (MD) data of Liew et al. (2008).
stated_limitations: Isothermal linear beam wave analysis; requires cut-off wavenumber (~10 nm^-1) at very high wavenumbers where phase velocity drops sharply.
future_work: Apply higher-order nonlocal strain-gradient framework to broader nanostructure mechanics (shells, plates, BCs) beyond 1D CNT beam wave dispersion.

title: Nonlocal elasticity of Klein-Gordon type: fundamentals and wave propagation
authors: Markus Lazar; Eleni Agiasofitou
read_scope: title, abstract, Secs. 1-2 (pp. 1-8), Sec. 4 dispersion/velocities (pp. 18-19), Sec. 5 conclusions & Appendix A (pp. 22-31)
model_constitutive: 3D linear elasticity with separable space-time nonlocality t_ij = alpha(x,t) * sigma_ij(x,t), where weak nonlocal operator is the Klein-Gordon operator L = 1 - l^2 Laplacian + (l^2/c^2) d^2/dt^2 (4 parameters: lambda, mu, length l, nonlocal speed c or time tau=l/c); isothermal.
geometry: 3D unbounded homogeneous isotropic elastic continuum
method: Green's function derivation of retarded Klein-Gordon dynamical kernels in 1D/2D/3D, Fourier transform dispersion analysis yielding quadratic in omega^2 for longitudinal and transverse waves
main_result: Fourth-order time derivative arises naturally from Klein-Gordon space-time nonlocality, predicting both acoustic (LA, TA) and positive-group-velocity optic (LO, TO) branches separated by a frequency band-gap using only 3 displacement DOFs and 4 parameters, provided c_L < c.
validation: Recovers Eringen Helmholtz spatial nonlocal elasticity as c -> infinity (tau -> 0) and classical elasticity as l -> 0; proves real positive omega^2 for all real k iff c_j < c (Appendix A).
stated_limitations: Restricted to unbounded isothermal homogeneous elastic continua; initial-boundary value problems and finite-domain modified kernels explicitly declared out of scope.
future_work: Initial-boundary value problems, finite-domain kernels, and anisotropic/coupled-field extensions (not solved in this paper).

title: Electromagnetic Waves Propagation in Graphene Multilayered Structures
authors: Mohammed M. Shabat; Muin F. Ubeid
model_constitutive: Macroscopic linear Maxwell equations for s-polarized (TE) monochromatic electromagnetic waves; graphene modeled as thin lossy dielectric slab of thickness d_g = N_g * 0.34 nm with complex refractive index n_g = 3 + i(C/3)lambda (C = 5.446 um^-1); no mechanics or heat.
geometry: 1D N-period graphene/dielectric (CaF2) multilayer stack embedded between vacuum half-spaces under oblique TE incidence
method: Snell's law, tangential E/H interface matching, Fresnel coefficients, and Vigoureux recursive transfer relation
main_result: Computes reflectance R', transmittance T', and graphene loss power P_loss = 1 - R' - T' vs wavelength (100-1700 nm), incidence angle, CaF2 thickness, and graphene layer count (1-3 monolayers).
validation: Energy conservation identity R' + T' + P_loss = 1 checked across all numerical examples.
stated_limitations: Purely optical/electromagnetic TE multilayer calculation using empirical visible-range refractive index for graphene; no thermoelastic or mechanical coupling.
future_work: Potential use in optical filters/biosensors hinted at end of conclusions.

title: A Note on Non-simple Heat Conduction
authors: Peter J. Chen; Morton E. Gurtin; William O. Williams
journal: Zeitschrift fur angewandte Mathematik und Physik (ZAMP)
model_constitutive: Steady-state linearized Chen-Gurtin two-temperature rigid heat conductor: q = -k grad phi, theta = phi - a Laplacian phi (isotropic, a > 0) and centrosymmetric anisotropic counterpart q = -K grad phi, theta = phi - lambda K : grad grad phi.
geometry: 3D rigid conductor (with 1D experimental slab/bar specialization noted)
method: Direct algebraic elimination between div q = r and two-temperature relation
main_result: Proves that in steady state the difference between thermodynamic and conductive temperatures is directly proportional to external heat supply: theta - phi = (a/k) r (or lambda r in anisotropic centrosymmetric media), vanishing when r = 0.
validation: Recovers theta = phi when external heat supply r = 0.
stated_limitations: Restricted to time-independent (steady-state) rigid heat conductors.
future_work: Suggests 1D steady controllable-radiation experiment to detect whether the two-temperature discrepancy a > 0 exists physically.

title: On the Thermodynamics of Non-simple Elastic Materials with Two Temperatures
authors: Peter J. Chen; Morton E. Gurtin; William O. Williams
journal: Zeitschrift fur angewandte Mathematik und Physik (ZAMP)
model_constitutive: Nonlinear and linearized two-temperature thermoelasticity (Chen-Gurtin-Williams): nonlinear response depends on F, VF, VVF and phi, Vphi, VVphi; linearized isotropic theory has S = lambda(tr E)I + 2mu E - alpha(3lambda+2mu)(phi - phi_0 - a Laplacian phi)I, q = -k grad phi, theta = phi - a Laplacian phi.
geometry: General 3D elastic body, specialized to steady free expansion of a cylinder of length l under uniform radiation r
method: Modified two-temperature Clausius-Duhem inequality (Coleman-Noll exploitation) and infinitesimal linearization
main_result: Shows two temperatures permit higher-grade dependence thermodynamically, yet linearized isotropic theory is mechanically simple (no strain gradients) and yields coupled PDEs where steady heat supply r induces an extra pressure p = beta*r and volume-change offset.
validation: Reduces to classical linear thermoelasticity when temperature discrepancy a = 0 (or steady r = 0).
stated_limitations: Proofs of nonlinear thermodynamic theorems omitted as analogous to Chen-Gurtin (1968); linearized theory remains parabolic/mechanical-simple without finite thermal wave speed.
future_work: Proposes steady-state radiation-induced free volume expansion of a cylinder as an experimental way to measure temperature discrepancy a.

title: On the Clausius-Duhem Inequality
authors: Morton E. Gurtin; William O. Williams
journal: Zeitschrift fur angewandte Mathematik und Physik (ZAMP)
model_constitutive: Axiomatic continuum thermodynamics with modified two-temperature Second Law d/dt int eta dm >= int (r/phi) dm - int (q.n/theta) da, tested on 'thermally regular' local constitutive classes and simple materials with fading memory.
geometry: General 3D deformable continuum B
method: Axiomatic measure-theoretic formulation and Coleman-Noll-type variational/Frechet-derivative contradiction proof
main_result: Proves that for any thermally regular constitutive class—including simple elastic materials with fading memory—compatibility with the two-temperature Second Law forces surface temperature theta and volume temperature phi to be identical, recovering the classical Clausius-Duhem inequality.
validation: Logical recovery of classical single-temperature Clausius-Duhem inequality for simple materials.
stated_limitations: Applies to thermally regular/simple materials; non-simple materials depending on higher spatial gradients violate thermal regularity and can sustain theta != phi.
future_work: Points to forthcoming full axiomatic paper (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 1967) and motivates non-simple two-temperature theories.

title: On a Theory of Heat Conduction Involving Two Temperatures
authors: Peter J. Chen; Morton E. Gurtin
journal: Zeitschrift fur angewandte Mathematik und Physik (ZAMP)
read_scope: title, intro, thermodynamic derivation & linearization (pp. 614-621), example plots & references (pp. 625-627)
model_constitutive: Rigid non-simple two-temperature heat conductor: e, s, theta, q depend on (phi, grad phi, grad^2 phi); linearized isotropic PDE c phi_t = k Laplacian phi + c*a Laplacian phi_t + r with theta = phi - a Laplacian phi (k > 0, a >= 0).
geometry: 3D rigid heat conductor; canonical progressive waves, acceleration/discontinuity fronts, and 1D semi-infinite bar under step boundary temperature
method: Coleman-Noll exploitation of two-temperature entropy inequality, material-symmetry tensor representation, energy uniqueness proof, harmonic/discontinuity analysis, Laplace/analytical step-heating solution
main_result: Proves A(phi) = lambda(phi) K(phi) >= 0; spatial derivative jumps in e and q decay exponentially as exp(-kt/(ca)) rather than vanishing instantaneously, and backward-in-time problem is stable for a > 0.
validation: Recovers classical Fourier heat equation as temperature discrepancy a -> 0 (shown in Figs. 2-3 for semi-infinite bar).
stated_limitations: Rigid heat conductor only (no elastic deformation); third-order mixed derivative Laplacian phi_t still gives non-hyperbolic propagation.
future_work: Extension to deformable thermoelastic materials (carried out in Chen, Gurtin & Williams 1969).

title: On surface waves in generalized thermoelasticity
authors: V. K. Agarwal
model_constitutive: 3D homogeneous isotropic linear generalized thermoelasticity of Lord-Shulman (relaxation tau) and Green-Lindsay (two constants alpha >= alpha* > 0) with surface thermal radiation BC theta_,3 + h*theta = 0.
geometry: 3D homogeneous isotropic half-space (x3 >= 0) with traction-free, radiating/isothermal/insulated plane boundary
method: Extension of Knowles (1966) and Carroll (1974) Lame-potential surface-wave representation theorem for general (non-plane) harmonic surface waves
main_result: Proves free harmonic thermoelastic surface waves in LS and GL half-spaces are governed by a single 2D surface wave potential satisfying the 2D Helmholtz equation, yield elliptical particle paths in spatially varying planes, and share identical secular equations when alpha = alpha* = tau.
validation: Reduces to Carroll (1974) classical thermoelastic surface waves when tau = 0 (or alpha = alpha* = 0), to Nayfeh & Nemat-Nasser (1971) when h = 0, and to classical Rayleigh equation when epsilon = 0.
stated_limitations: Analytical secular equation derived and compared structurally, without numerical root-finding across parameter regimes.
future_work: None explicitly stated.

title: Thermodynamics with Internal State Variables
authors: Bernard D. Coleman; Morton E. Gurtin
read_scope: title, abstract, Secs. 1-3 (pp. 597-599), Sec. 14 ideal-gas example & conclusion (p. 613)
model_constitutive: Nonlinear thermoelastic continua with N internal ('hidden') state variables alpha = (alpha_1,...,alpha_N) governed by ODEs dot(alpha) = f(theta, F, grad theta, alpha) alongside psi, eta, T, q depending on (theta, F, grad theta, alpha).
geometry: General 3D nonlinear deformable heat-conducting body (and ideal gas with internal vibrational mode)
method: Coleman-Noll Clausius-Duhem exploitation, Lyapunov/nonlinear ODE asymptotic stability theory at fixed (F, theta), integral dissipation inequalities
main_result: Establishes thermodynamic identities T = rho d_F psi, eta = -d_theta psi, d_grad_theta psi = 0, internal dissipation d_alpha psi . f <= 0, Lyapunov role of free energy at equilibrium, conditions for internal-mode temperatures, and relaxing ideal-gas specialization.
validation: Recovers classical thermostatics at internal equilibrium and classical relaxing polyatomic ideal-gas vibrational relaxation equations (Bethe-Teller/Landau-Teller).
stated_limitations: Finite internal state variables yield discrete relaxation spectra when linearized (less suited than fading-memory functionals for broad polymer spectra); body couples and mass diffusion excluded.
future_work: Foundation for internal-variable theories of dissipation, relaxation, and generalized heat/viscoplastic models.

title: Propagation of shear waves in an irregular magnetoelastic monoclinic layer sandwiched between two isotropic half-spaces
authors: A. Chattopadhyay; S. Gupta; A. K. Singh; S. A. Sahu
journal: International Journal of Engineering, Science and Technology
read_scope: title, abstract, formulation (pp. 228-232), numerical plots & conclusion (pp. 240-244)
model_constitutive: Perfectly conducting linear magnetoelastic monoclinic crystal layer (Lorentz body force J x B, linearized Maxwell stress, sigma -> infinity, displacement current neglected) between two isotropic elastic half-spaces; isothermal.
geometry: 2D/antiplane sandwiched monoclinic layer (-H <= y <= epsilon*h(z)) with small rectangular lower-interface irregularity between two isotropic elastic half-spaces
method: Fourier transform, Eringen-Samuels (1959) first-order boundary perturbation in epsilon = H'/s << 1, contour integration
main_result: Closed-form perturbed Love-type SH dispersion relation showing phase velocity c/beta_2 decreases as rectangular irregularity depth H'/H or magnetoelastic monoclinic parameter m_H increases.
validation: Reduces to classical isotropic Love-type sandwiched-layer dispersion relation when magnetic field, monoclinic anisotropy, and interface irregularity vanish.
stated_limitations: First-order perturbation valid only for small irregularity aspect ratio epsilon = H'/s << 1, perfectly conducting assumption (sigma -> infinity), isothermal SH polarization only.
future_work: Geophysical seismic interpretation across irregular crustal/continental-margin layers.

title: Reflection and Transmission of Elastic Waves at Viscous Liquid/Micropolar Elastic Solid Interface
authors: Rajneesh Kumar; Sushil K. Tomar
journal: International Journal of Mathematics and Mathematical Sciences
model_constitutive: 2D linear Eringen micropolar elastic solid (potentials phi, U, Phi; longitudinal wave and two coupled transverse-microrotation waves for omega^2/omega_0^2 > 2) welded to compressible Navier-Stokes viscous liquid; isothermal.
geometry: Plane interface z = 0 separating viscous liquid half-space (z < 0) and isotropic micropolar elastic half-space (z > 0)
method: Helmholtz potential decomposition, Snell's law, 5x5 complex linear interface BC system solved numerically for reflection/refraction amplitude ratios
main_result: Computes amplitude ratios Z1..Z5 vs incidence angle (0-90 deg) for incident longitudinal or coupled transverse-microrotation waves, demonstrating measurable liquid-viscosity effects on reflected/refracted amplitudes.
validation: Reduces analytically to inviscid-liquid/micropolar-solid interface solution of Tomar & Kumar (1995) when viscosity eta -> 0; uses Gauthier aluminum-epoxy micropolar data.
stated_limitations: Isothermal 2D plane-harmonic analysis; energy-flux conservation balance across the dissipative viscous interface is not checked.
future_work: Potential application to water-mud-rock or crust-mantle seismological interfaces.

title: Bleustein-Gulyaev waves in some functionally graded materials
authors: Bernard Collet; Michel Destrade; Gerard A. Maugin
model_constitutive: Quasi-electrostatic linear piezoacoustics in a functionally graded 6mm hexagonal piezoelectric half-space with co-proportional depth grading {c44, e15, eps11, rho}(x2) = {c44^0, e15^0, eps11^0, rho^0} f(x2); isothermal.
geometry: Semi-infinite 6mm piezoelectric half-space (x2 >= 0) with traction-free electrically free or metallized surface
method: Liouville-type rescaling u_hat = sqrt(f) u decoupling 4x4 first-order system into constant-coefficient 2nd-order ODEs, plus Varley-Seymour hierarchy generating infinitely many exact solvable profiles f(x2)
main_result: Derives exact closed-form Bleustein-Gulyaev surface-wave speed, depth profiles, and electromechanical coupling K_S^2 for exponential, algebraic (beta*x2+1)^+-2, hyperbolic/trigonometric, and asymptotically homogeneous tanh^2 profiles.
validation: Recovers classical homogeneous Bleustein-Gulyaev (1968/1969) solution as grading parameter beta -> 0 (PZT-4 ceramic examples).
stated_limitations: Explicitly notes that proportional grading of mass density rho(x2) alongside c44, e15, eps11 is physically restrictive/unlikely, adopted so exact elementary-function benchmarks exist; isothermal anti-plane SH only.
future_work: Use exact analytical solutions as benchmarks for BEM/numerical solvers when density and stiffness/piezoelectric moduli have independent depth profiles.

title: Considerations of the existence of interfacial (Stoneley) waves in bonded anisotropic elastic half-spaces
authors: D. M. Barnett; J. Lothe; S. D. Gavazza; M. J. P. Musgrave
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London A
model_constitutive: Classical linear anisotropic elasticity C_ijkl(1), C_ijkl(2) in two welded half-spaces via Stroh formalism and Hermitian surface impedance tensors Z(1), Z(2) forming interface impedance tensor Lambda(v) = Z(1) + Z*(2)
geometry: Two bonded dissimilar arbitrarily anisotropic elastic half-spaces separated by planar interface n.x = 0
method: Stroh six-dimensional surface-wave synthesis, Hermitian surface/interface impedance eigenvalue monotonicity analysis, and numerical limiting-speed root search on tilted cubic copper bi-crystals
main_result: Proves that at most one subsonic Stoneley wave exists (uniqueness), establishes necessary and sufficient algebraic existence criterion at v = min(v_hat(1), v_hat(2)) via det(Lambda) < 0 or (tr Lambda)^2 - tr(Lambda^2) < 0, proves v_s >= min Rayleigh wave speed, and formulates subsonic slip-wave secular equation n.[Z^-1(1)+Z^-1(2)].n = 0
validation: Analytical limiting-speed bounds and 5- to 7-significant-figure numerical computations for twisted/tilted cubic Cu bi-crystal interfaces
stated_limitations: Restricted to subsonic regime 0 <= v < min(v_hat(1), v_hat(2)) and linear isothermal elastic media; for small misorientations v_s differs from limiting speed only in the 3rd-4th significant digit
future_work: Analyze transition rays separating allowed and forbidden Stoneley sectors; investigate supersonic Stoneley modes (v_s > v_hat(1)); complete full study of anisotropic slip-wave non-uniqueness (0, 1, or 2 modes)

title: The Range of Existence of Rayleigh and Stoneley Waves
authors: J. G. Scholte
journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, Geophysical Supplement
model_constitutive: Classical linear isotropic compressible elasticity (Lame constants lambda, mu and lambda', mu', densities rho, rho')
geometry: Welded interface between two semi-infinite isotropic media (T/L -> inf) and superficial isotropic elastic layer of finite thickness T over a half-space
method: Exact algebraic analysis of Stoneley and layered-Rayleigh secular determinant boundary curves and asymptotic T/L approximations
main_result: Determines exact closed-form boundary curves in (rho/rho', mu/mu') parameter space enclosing the existence domain of Stoneley waves (generalizing Wiechert's condition) and maps regions admitting 0, 1, or 2 generalized Rayleigh/Stoneley surface wave systems for finite T/L
validation: Analytical limiting-case checks against Love (incompressible), Bromwich (thin-layer T/L -> 0), and Stoneley (1924) and explicit existence diagrams (Figs. 1-8)
stated_limitations: Asymptotic approximation of existence boundaries fails for very small T/L where thin-layer expansions must be used instead; purely elastic isothermal isotropic media
future_work: None explicitly stated beyond applying the asymptotic existence-curve method to geophysical layered media

title: Thermodynamic Restrictions on the Relaxation Functions of the Theory of Heat Conduction with Finite Wave Speeds
authors: Peter J. Chen; Jace W. Nunziato
journal: Zeitschrift fur angewandte Mathematik und Physik (ZAMP)
model_constitutive: Gurtin-Pipkin rigid heat conductor with memory: linearized hyperbolic integrodifferential heat equation with internal energy relaxation function beta(s) and heat-flux relaxation function alpha(s)
geometry: Rigid isotropic/anisotropic heat-conducting continuum (arbitrary 3D body)
method: Clausius-Duhem inequality exploitation along smooth continuation histories of temperature and summed temperature-gradient history with fading memory
main_result: Proves from the Second Law alone that equilibrium heat flux vanishes, initial heat-flux relaxation slope alpha'(0) <= 0, and equilibrium conductivity integral int_0^inf alpha(s) ds >= 0 (with alpha(0) >= 0 from free-energy minimality), justifying wave-propagation and uniqueness hypotheses
validation: Rigorous thermodynamic theorem-proof consistency check against Coleman fading-memory thermodynamics and Gurtin-Pipkin (1968)
stated_limitations: Rigid heat conductor (no mechanical deformation coupling); shows Second Law alone does not restrict initial value alpha(0) >= 0 without an extra minimal free-energy postulate at equilibrium
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Stability in Thermoelasticity of Type III
authors: Ramon Quintanilla; Reinhard Racke
journal: Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems - Series B
model_constitutive: Linearized Green-Naghdi Type III hyperbolic thermoelasticity: u_tt - alpha u_xx + beta theta_x = 0, theta_tt - delta theta_xx + gamma u_ttx - kappa theta_txx = 0 (and 2D/3D anisotropic/inhomogeneous forms)
geometry: Bounded 1D interval (0, L) with Dirichlet/Neumann thermal BCs, radially symmetric 2D/3D bounded domains Omega, and general anisotropic 3D domains
method: Lyapunov multiplier energy functionals, spectral asymptotic root analysis, and Cesaro time-averaged Lagrange-identity energy equipartition estimates
main_result: Proves exponential decay of total energy in 1D (for u=theta=0 and u=theta_x=0) and in radially symmetric 2D/3D domains (curl u = 0), and establishes O(1/t) asymptotic equipartition between time-averaged kinetic and potential/thermal energies in general anisotropic 3D Type III media
validation: Rigorous analytical PDE proofs and comparison with Zhang & Zuazua (2003) and classical/second-sound thermoelasticity decay rates
stated_limitations: Uniform exponential decay fails in general multi-dimensional domains when curl u != 0 (shear waves remain undamped, just as in classical thermoelasticity); existence proofs omitted as standard
future_work: Extend energy equipartition and decay analyses to alternative mechanical/thermal boundary conditions (Remark 6)

title: Elastic metasurfaces for splitting SV- and P-waves in elastic solids
authors: Xiaoshi Su; Zhaocheng Lu; Andrew N. Norris
model_constitutive: Classical linear isotropic elastodynamics in bulk half-spaces coupled to Mindlin thick-plate waveguides with shear and rotary-inertia correction factors (kappa, lambda)
geometry: 2D elastic solid containing a periodic/graded array of parallel rectangular slit cracks forming variable-thickness plate-like waveguides connecting two half-spaces
method: Symmetric/antisymmetric 3x3 modal matching at slit junctions for explicit transmission/phase formulas combined with Generalized Snell's Law and 2D COMSOL full-wave FEM
main_result: Achieves full 2*pi transmitted phase control for normally incident SV-waves via plate thickness grading while leaving normally incident P-wave phase nearly unchanged, demonstrating mode-conversion-free SV/P wave splitting and planar/cylindrical SV-wave focusing lenses around 60 kHz
validation: Full-wave 2D COMSOL finite-element simulations matching analytical transmission/phase curves and focal distances (25.7 cm vs 25 cm design for plane SV wave)
stated_limitations: Analytical unit-cell model neglects P-SV mode conversion under oblique incidence, causing a 3.3 cm focal-length shift (28.3 cm vs 25 cm) for cylindrical SV sources; focal distance varies with frequency due to flexural dispersion
future_work: Improve the analytical transmission model to incorporate oblique-incidence P-SV mode conversion at slit junctions

title: Analysis of SH wave in hollow piezo-composite cylinder with coupled imperfect interface condition
authors: Shreeta Kumari; Sanjeev A. Sahu; Kamlesh K. Pankaj
journal: Mechanics Based Design of Structures and Machines
model_constitutive: Linear pre-stressed transversely isotropic piezoelectric (PE), piezomagnetic (PM), and helically fiber-reinforced (FR) elasticity with coupled mechanical-electrical-magnetic spring-type imperfect interfaces (K0..K6)
geometry: Three-layer concentric hollow cylinder: inner fiber-reinforced cylinder (r0..r1), middle piezomagnetic cylinder (r1..r2), and outer piezoelectric cylinder (r2..r3)
method: Circumferential SH-wave Bessel-function potential expansion and 14x14 boundary/interface determinant dispersion analysis under EOMS and ESMO circuit conditions
main_result: Derives closed-form determinant dispersion relations for circumferential SH modes (1st and 2nd modes) under EOMS and ESMO conditions and quantifies sensitivity to mechanical, electrical, magnetic, and cross-coupled interface imperfections, circumferential initial stresses, thickness ratios, and fiber helix angle
validation: Analytical limiting-case reductions to perfectly bonded and simpler layered cylindrical SH-wave benchmarks plus parametric dispersion curves for two modes
stated_limitations: Isothermal, linear, decoupled antiplane SH polarization only; no experimental comparison
future_work: Extend the hollow piezo-composite SAW cylinder model to structures submerged in viscous liquids or with solid-filled cores and experimental sensor optimization

title: The Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation with memory in the critical case
authors: Filippo Dell'Oro; Irena Lasiecka; Vittorino Pata
model_constitutive: Abstract linear Moore-Gibson-Thompson (MGT) viscoelastic/thermoacoustic equation with Type-I memory: u_ttt + alpha u_tt + beta A u_t + gamma A u - int_0^t g(s) A u(t-s) ds = 0 in the critical regime kappa = beta - gamma/alpha = 0
geometry: Abstract separable Hilbert space H with strictly positive selfadjoint operator A (covering bounded/unbounded PDE domains with Dirichlet/Neumann/Robin BCs)
method: History-space contraction semigroup formulation, Gearhart-Pruss/Batty-Borichev-Tomilov resolvent bounds on the imaginary axis
main_result: Proves a sharp dichotomy in the critical case alpha*beta = gamma with convex exponential-decay kernel g: the semigroup/Volterra energy is exponentially stable if and only if A is a bounded operator; when A is unbounded, uniform decay fails, but semiuniform stability (lim E(t)=0) and explicit polynomial decay rates hold for regular initial data
validation: Rigorous functional-analytic necessity and sufficiency proofs via spectral/resolvent blow-up sequences
stated_limitations: Linearized equation (k=0) with memory acting solely on u (w=u) and convex exponentially bounded kernel g satisfying (g1)-(g4)
future_work: Transfer higher-topological-level polynomial/semiuniform decay estimates toward critical-regime quasilinear MGT equations

title: On the Moore-Gibson-Thompson Equation and Its Relation to Linear Viscoelasticity
authors: Filippo Dell'Oro; Vittorino Pata
model_constitutive: Linear third-order Moore-Gibson-Thompson (MGT) PDE u_ttt + alpha u_tt - beta Delta u_t - gamma Delta u = 0 compared with second-order linear viscoelasticity with exponential relaxation kernel kappa(s) = a*exp(-b*s) + c
geometry: Bounded smooth domain Omega subset R^N with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions (abstract positive operator A = -Delta)
method: History-space semigroup decomposition and exact trajectory/initial-data correspondence mapping between viscoelasticity and MGT
main_result: Establishes precise non-bijective dynamical equivalence between MGT (in subcritical alpha*beta > gamma) and exponential-kernel viscoelasticity, proving an unexpected regularity-preservation and exponential decay property for viscoelastic trajectories satisfying a compatibility condition on initial history
validation: Rigorous operator-semigroup theorems and explicit counterexamples showing why general non-exponential kernels lose MGT equivalence
stated_limitations: Exact correspondence holds only for single-exponential memory kernels kappa(s) = a*exp(-b*s)+c and linear constant-coefficient operators
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: A Theory of Thermoelastic Materials with Voids
authors: D. Iesan
model_constitutive: Linear classical-Fourier coupled thermoelasticity with Cowin-Nunziato void volume-fraction field phi (anisotropic and isotropic formulations derived via Green-Rivlin energy invariance)
geometry: Arbitrary 3D bounded/unbounded porous thermoelastic body; acceleration wavefronts in isotropic media; static point heat source, thick spherical shell, and hollow cylinder
method: Green-Rivlin invariance derivation, Laplace-transform convolution reciprocity/variational principles (Gurtin type), Hadamard singular-surface compatibility/growth ODEs, and closed-form elastostatics
main_result: Establishes uniqueness (without definiteness of elasticity tensor for reciprocity), convolutional variational theorems, three acceleration wave speeds (longitudinal c1, transverse c2, compaction/distension c3) with explicit discontinuity-order couplings (2nd-order thermal, 3rd-order porosity), and exact static solutions for point heat source and pressurized/heated porous shells/cylinders
validation: Analytical reduction to Cowin-Nunziato isothermal void elasticity and classical thermoelasticity when void coupling vanishes
stated_limitations: Uses classical Fourier heat conduction (infinite thermal speed, so thermal field jumps only at 2nd/3rd order across mechanical acceleration fronts); infinitesimal linear deformations
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Rational Extended Thermodynamics (Second Edition)
authors: Ingo Muller; Tommaso Ruggeri
journal: Springer Tracts in Natural Philosophy, Vol. 37 (Monograph)
model_constitutive: Rational Extended Thermodynamics (RET) balance-law hierarchies with concave entropy and Liu Lagrange multipliers: Cattaneo/13-moment to arbitrary N-moment gases, mixtures, relativistic fluids, photons, phonons (Boltzmann-Peierls -> Guyer-Krumhansl & pure second sound, Ch. 14), metal electrons, and rate-type vs differential-type viscoelasticity (Ch. 16)
geometry: 3D continua, 1D plane harmonic waves, shock structures, light-scattering bulk media, NaF/Bi 1D crystal heat-pulse slabs, and radiative half-spaces/spheres
method: Symmetric hyperbolic conservation-law closure via entropy maximization, Galilean/Lorentz invariance, Maxwell iteration, dispersion/characteristic-speed analysis, and shock ODE integration
main_result: Demonstrates systematically that local balance-law moment hierarchies with concave nonequilibrium entropy yield causal symmetric hyperbolic PDEs with finite pulse speeds, resolving Fourier/Navier-Stokes/second-grade-fluid paradoxes and converging quantitatively to high-frequency ultrasound, light-scattering, shock-profile, and cryogenic NaF phonon second-sound experiments as moment order N increases
validation: Extensive quantitative comparisons with noble-gas ultrasound dispersion/attenuation, laser light-scattering dynamic form factors, Mach>1 shock profiles, and Jackson-Walker/McNelly cryogenic NaF ballistic + second-sound heat-pulse experiments (Ch. 14)
stated_limitations: Requires large moment hierarchies (20-84+ moments) at high Knudsen numbers/Mach numbers where subshocks appear; in viscoelasticity (Ch. 16.3.6), truncated balance-law stress-rate equations contain spin-dependent inertial terms violatingrheological material-frame indifference
future_work: Reconcile extended-thermodynamic rate-type viscoelasticity and boundary value prescriptions for high-order moment fluxes with continuum rheology and solid-state experiments

title: Thermoelasticity and Irreversible Thermodynamics
authors: M. A. Biot
model_constitutive: Classical linear coupled anisotropic and isotropic thermoelasticity derived from Onsager irreversible thermodynamics, generalized thermoelastic potential V, dissipation function D, and Fourier heat conduction
geometry: General 3D anisotropic/isotropic continuum, unbounded wave-propagation space, and 1D heated/vibrating thermoelastic plates
method: Variational Lagrangian principle in generalized coordinates (displacement u and entropy displacement S), operational admittance matrix / relaxation-spectrum representation, and poroelastic consolidation isomorphism
main_result: Formulates coupled linear thermoelasticity from irreversible thermodynamics, proves mathematical isomorphism with isothermal poroelastic consolidation, derives the thermoelastic admittance matrix (viscoelastic-like relaxation spectrum), notes infinite signal velocity of dilatational thermoelastic waves, and computes plate heating and flexural thermoelastic damping
validation: Closed-form normal-coordinate solutions for transient plate heating and vibrating-plate thermoelastic damping recovering Zener's damping formula
stated_limitations: Assumes classical Fourier law and Onsager linear near-equilibrium reciprocity, yielding parabolic-coupled dilatational waves with infinite signal speed
future_work: Apply generalized-coordinate variational and operational admittance methods to complex structural heat-conduction and thermoelastic-damping problems

title: A critical review of non-Fourier heat transfer theories with phase lag in bio-heating: Explaining the variations in reported phase lag coefficients
authors: Mohammad Azhdari; Ghader Rezazadeh; Raghav Pathak; Hans-Michael Tautenhahn; Franziska Tautenhahn; Tim Ricken; Seyed Morteza Seyedpour
model_constitutive: Systematic critical review of Cattaneo-Vernotte (CV/SPL), Dual-Phase-Lag (DPL), and Three-Phase-Lag (TPL) Pennes/bioheat conduction models across 110 papers (1995-2025)
geometry: Biological tissues, tissue-mimicking phantoms, multi-layer skin/tumor slabs, cylinders, and spheres under laser/hyperthermia heating
method: Systematic meta-analysis of 110 bio-heating studies, audit of experimental thermocouple/boundary-condition artifacts (Mitra et al., Antaki, Sahoo et al.), and scale-separation/ill-posedness critique (Auriault, Maillet, Rukolaine)
main_result: Finds extreme inconsistency in reported biological phase-lag values (near 0 s up to 32 s), showing that large macroscopic phase lags (>1 s) stem from experimental artifacts or unverified citation chains and can trigger DPL ill-posedness/negative temperatures, whereas rigorously controlled experiments yield near-zero macroscopic phase lags consistent with Fourier's law
validation: Cross-audit of 110 published parameter tables against independent replication experiments (Herwig & Beckert, Roetzel, Maillet, Azhdari et al.)
stated_limitations: Focuses on macroscopic bio-heating (CV, DPL, TPL heat transfer without thermoelastic wave coupling); ultrafast microscale laser regimes remain distinct
future_work: Establish standardized experimental calibration protocols, uncertainty/sensitivity analyses, and scale-consistent criteria before invoking phase-lag models in biomedical heating

title: Dynamic resource provisioning for service-based cloud applications: A Bayesian learning approach
authors: Reena Panwar; M. Supriya
journal: Journal of Parallel and Distributed Computing
model_constitutive: Off-topic computer science paper: IBM MAPE-K autonomic cloud control loop combining linear regression workload forecasting and Bayesian probabilistic learning for IaaS VM provisioning
geometry: Cloud data-center virtual machine (VM) service queues (not a continuum mechanics geometry)
method: Proactive-reactive Bayesian + linear regression auto-scaling algorithms simulated in CloudSim on real-world Google Cluster and ClarkNet workload traces
main_result: Reduces overall cloud provisioning cost by up to 31%, increases resource utilization by 12%, and lowers response time, RMSE, VM count, and SLA rejection rates compared to fuzzy-logic MAPE-K baselines
validation: CloudSim trace-driven simulations benchmarked against fuzzy-autonomic provisioning on ClarkNet and Google Cluster logs
stated_limitations: Off-topic to thermoelasticity/wave mechanics; evaluated in CloudSim trace simulation rather than live multi-cloud deployment
future_work: Combine the Bayesian MAPE-K provisioning framework with metaheuristic optimization and hybrid fuzzy-probabilistic controllers

title: On a multi-phase-lag model of coupled thermoelasticity
authors: A. M. Zenkour; H. F. El-Mekawy
journal: International Communications in Heat and Mass Transfer
model_constitutive: Unified higher-order Refined Multi-Phase-Lag (RPL) anisotropic coupled thermoelasticity (M-th order Taylor expansion in tau_q, N-th order in tau_theta and tau_vartheta, plus Green-Lindsay stress/entropy relaxation tau_1) coupled to carrier plasma diffusion in photothermal semiconductor beams
geometry: General 3D anisotropic solid for constitutive derivation; clamped/simply-supported isotropic photothermal semiconducting Euler-Bernoulli micro/nanobeam under ramped/harmonic heating for validation
method: Higher-order Taylor phase-lag unification hierarchy and analytical Laplace-transform / normal-mode beam bending solution
main_result: Constructs a single higher-order multi-phase-lag coupled heat equation that reduces as special cases to CTE, LS, GL, GN-II, GN-III, Tzou DPL, and Roy Choudhuri TPL, and compares axial/through-thickness deflection, temperature, stress, and carrier density in a semiconducting beam
validation: Parametric reduction comparisons across CTE, LS, GN, DPL, and RPL limits on a silicon-like photothermal beam
stated_limitations: Relies on formal higher-order Taylor polynomial truncations (M, N up to higher orders) without proving semigroup well-posedness or Herglotz/Hurwitz root stability for arbitrary M, N
future_work: Apply the unified higher-order RPL model to microstructural and photothermal multi-field structural problems

title: The impact of periodicity in functionally graded materials on the attenuation of elastic shear waves
authors: Xuhui Li; Jun Shen; Chenliang Li; Zailin Yang; Minghe Li
model_constitutive: Classical 2D linear elastodynamics for antiplane SH waves in continuously inhomogeneous functionally graded materials (FGM) with trigonometric periodic shear modulus mu(x,y) and density rho(x,y)
geometry: 2D half-space / foundation isolation region with trigonometric periodic spatial grading under incident harmonic SH seismic waves
method: Liouville-type amplitude scaling W = mu^(-1/2)*phi reducing the variable-coefficient SH equation to Helmholtz form in complex coordinates (z, z_bar), analytical wavefield series, and parametric optimization over grading frequency beta
main_result: Finds optimal spatial grading periodicity (beta = 1.26, related to incident quarter-wavelength/frequency) that aligns high local wave impedance with stress peaks, folding down peak SH displacement by 20.34% relative to homogeneous media
validation: Analytical reduction to homogeneous half-space limit and parametric 2D/3D wavefield and stress comparisons across grading profiles
stated_limitations: Purely elastic (undamped, no viscoelastic memory), isothermal, and restricted to scalar antiplane SH waves (no coupled P-SV conversion)
future_work: Incorporate viscoelastic memory variables for material damping and extend periodic FGM attenuation analysis to coupled P and SV waves for multidimensional seismic ground motion

title: Thermal Relaxation Times Effect on Rayleigh Waves in Generalized Thermoelastic Media
authors: Abo-el-nour N. Abd-Alla; Amira A. S. Al-Dawy
model_constitutive: Isotropic linear generalized thermoelasticity comparing Classical Dynamical Coupled (C-D), Lord-Shulman (L-S, tau_0), and Green-Lindsay (G-L, tau_1 >= tau_0 > 0) theories
geometry: Homogeneous isotropic thermally insulated traction-free half-space z >= 0
method: Helmholtz potential decomposition (P-thermal coupled 4th-order ODE + decoupled SV 2nd-order ODE), normal-mode secular determinant, and numerical root/depth-profile computation
main_result: Derives the unified C-D/L-S/G-L Rayleigh wave secular determinant for an insulated free surface, showing thermal relaxation lowers elastic wave speed, G-L approaches L-S as tau_1 -> tau_0, tau_1 > tau_0 strongly modifies surface amplitudes, and depth decay is non-oscillatory
validation: Analytical recovery of Lockett (1958) classical thermoelastic Rayleigh waves and Nayfeh & Nemat-Nasser (1971) L-S Rayleigh waves as limiting cases
stated_limitations: Restricted to homogeneous isotropic half-space with thermally insulated boundary (dT/dz = 0) and L-S/G-L models only
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Linear Theory of Nonlocal Elasticity and Dispersion of Plane Waves
authors: A. Cemal Eringen
model_constitutive: Integral linear nonlocal elasticity t_kl(x) = int_V [lambda'(|x-x'|) e_rr(x') delta_kl + 2*mu'(|x-x'|) e_kl(x')] dv(x') linearized from Eringen-Edelen nonlocal continuum thermodynamics
geometry: General 3D inhomogeneous/homogeneous nonlocal body for linearization; infinite 1D medium / periodic atomic chain for plane harmonic waves
method: Frechet-derivative linearization of nonlocal free-energy functional, proof of vanishing nonlocal body-force residual in stress-free natural state, and Fourier-transform kernel inversion against Born-von Karman N-neighbor lattice dispersion
main_result: Proves that nonlocal body-force residuals vanish in homogeneous isotropic linear nonlocal elasticity and determines explicit closed-form cosine/sine-integral nonlocal kernel alpha(|x-x'|) matching 1D N-neighbor lattice phonon dispersion exactly across the entire Brillouin zone
validation: Comparison with 1D Brillouin nearest-neighbor dispersion, Yarnell et al. experimental Al (100)/(110) phonon branches (1-2% fit with 8-15 neighbors), and Harrison Al ion-ion pair potential
stated_limitations: Exact 1D Fourier kernel inversion assumes an infinite medium; footnote explicitly warns that for bodies with finite boundaries, reducing 3D nonlocal integrals requires extra boundary-layer care
future_work: Extend nonlocal dispersion calibration to 3D anisotropic crystals and finite-boundary problems

title: Theory of Nonlocal Thermoelasticity
authors: A. Cemal Eringen
model_constitutive: Spatial-integral linear nonlocal thermoelasticity (anisotropic and isotropic) with nonlocal elastic moduli (lambda', mu'), nonlocal thermomechanical coupling beta'(|x-x'|), nonlocal thermal capacity gamma'(|x-x'|), and nonlocal Fourier conductivity kappa'(|x-x'|), instantaneous in time (no thermal relaxation times)
geometry: Arbitrary 3D finite thermoelastic body V with boundary S and internal discontinuity/crack surface sigma
method: Hilbert-space Frechet thermodynamics under restored Axiom of Objectivity and Axiom of Nonlocality, eliminating nonlocal mass/energy/body-force residuals and integrating by parts via Green-Gauss theorem
main_result: Derives residual-free coupled field equations (5.13)-(5.14) for displacement u_k and temperature T in linear nonlocal thermoelasticity, proving nonlocal mass and energy residuals vanish (h_hat = 0) and showing boundary/crack surface integrals naturally encode surface stress, surface tension, and surface heat
validation: Reduces exactly to Eringen (1972) isothermal nonlocal elasticity and classical local Biot thermoelasticity in the Dirac-delta kernel limit
stated_limitations: Purely spatial nonlocality with instantaneous (parabolic-type) heat conduction (no Cattaneo/phase-lag/memory relaxation); no concrete boundary-value or wave-propagation problem solved in the paper
future_work: Solve concrete finite-boundary thermoelastic surface-physics, crack, and lattice phonon-dispersion problems in subsequent works

title: Update on a class of gradient theories
authors: E. C. Aifantis
model_constitutive: Aifantis single/two-length-scale gradient elasticity (sigma = C:epsilon - c*Laplacian(C:epsilon) and implicit stress-gradient extensions), strain-gradient plasticity (tau = kappa(gamma) - c*Laplacian(gamma)), reaction-diffusion defect kinetics, and wavelet-transformed scale-dependent constitutive laws
geometry: Screw/edge dislocations near interfaces, crack tips, bimetallic/coherent interfaces, sheared boundary layers (-H/2, H/2), micron-sized twisted wires, micro/nano-indentation half-spaces, and smooth tensile micro-bars
method: Ru-Aifantis operator factorization, Maxwell equal-area nonlinear interface construction, strength-of-materials torsion/indentation scaling, and discrete wavelet + stochastic cellular-automata analysis
main_result: Synthesizes gradient elasticity/plasticity solutions eliminating dislocation and crack-tip strain/stress singularities, capturing boundary layers and Fleck et al. micro-wire torsion / Nix-Gao nano-indentation size effects with a single internal length l_c ~ 5-6 um, and introduces wavelet scale-dependent laws for gradient-free uniform tension size effects
validation: Quantitative fits to Fleck et al. (1994) Cu micro-wire torsion data, Nix & Gao (1998) nano-indentation hardness data, and SFM slip-band step profiles in Fe3Al
stated_limitations: Static/quasi-static isothermal mechanics only; higher-order interfacial boundary-condition selection (continuous strain gradient vs flux-like l^2*mu*dgamma/dy) changes interface predictions; uniform tensile size effects cannot be captured by pure Laplacian terms without internal-variable or wavelet modification
future_work: Calibrate gradient coefficients directly from 3D discrete dislocation dynamics (DDD) and atomistic Rose-Ferrante-Smith potentials, and test wavelet scale-dependent constitutive predictions across tension, bending, and torsion

title: On the Role of Gradients in the Localization of Deformation and Fracture
authors: Elias C. Aifantis
model_constitutive: Strain-gradient viscoplasticity (tau = kappa(gamma, gamma_dot) - c*Laplacian(gamma)) with diffusive back-stress evolution and Aifantis strain-gradient linear elasticity sigma = lambda*tr(epsilon)I + 2*mu*epsilon - c*Laplacian[lambda*tr(epsilon)I + 2*mu*epsilon]
geometry: 1D/2D softening shear bands, periodic persistent slip bands (PSBs), propagating Luders and Portevin-Le Chatelier (PLC) tensile bands, and Mode-III antiplane sharp crack in an infinite medium
method: Linear/nonlinear Turing-type wavelength selection, Lienard relaxation-oscillation traveling waves, Fourier-transform Mode-III crack solution, and Ru-Aifantis operator reduction (1 - c*Laplacian)u = u_0
main_result: Shows strain gradients regularize post-localization softening (giving analytical shear-band width, PSB wavelength, and Luders/PLC band speeds) and proves via exact Mode-III crack solution that gradient elasticity eliminates crack-tip strain singularity and yields smooth Barenblatt cohesive-zone crack-face closure without ad hoc cohesive tractions
validation: Qualitative and semi-quantitative comparison with Cu monocrystal PSB spacing, adiabatic double-hump shear bands (Giovanola 1988), and Al-5%Mg PLC band speeds
stated_limitations: Classical Cauchy stress remains singular at the crack tip under pure strain-gradient elasticity (even though strain is finite); higher-order boundary conditions (e.g., d^2 u / dn^2 = 0) require physical justification; isothermal only
future_work: Determine gradient coefficients directly from elastic-plastic bending experiments and dislocation pileup/cross-slip micromechanics, and extend crack-tip gradient elasticity to Modes I-II, interfacial cracks, and nonlinear curved/zig-zag fracture patterns
